blocks.title: Free radical
blocks.text: A free radical is a species that has one or more unpaired electrons.

A simple example is the free chlorine atom, with the configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5: in the 3p subshell two orbitals hold paired electrons and the third holds a single unpaired electron, shown by a dot after the symbol. Apart from single atoms, groups of atoms can also be free radicals, for example the hydroxyl radical OH and the methyl radical CH3.

blocks.prompt: Write the configurations of the aluminium radical (Z = 13) and the copper radical (Z = 29) and say where the unpaired electron is in each.
blocks.explanation: Aluminium is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1, with its single unpaired electron in 3p. Copper is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s1, with the unpaired electron in 4s. Each atom, having one unpaired electron, is a free radical.

items: A free radical has one or more unpaired electrons, shown by a dot: the chlorine atom (one unpaired 3p electron), OH, CH3.
